title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from p. 82): K is a subfield of C with algebraic closure K̄ in C and Γ = Gal(K̄/K). X and Y are K-varieties. Π_1(X) is the topological fundamental groupoid of X(C), and Π̂_1(X) is its profinite completion. Π̂_1 can be identified with the étale fundamental groupoid. Restricted to points of X(K̄), it carries an action of Γ: ℓ ↦ ^uℓ. For a path ℓ between K-rational points (the notation X_K for rational points), earlier pages attach Galois-theoretic invariants f_ℓ(u), g_ℓ(u). Presumably these are the 'discrepancies' (^uℓ)·ℓ^{-1} or ℓ^{-1}·(^uℓ), lying in the profinite fundamental group at the endpoint (resp. the origin), and they behave like non-abelian 1-cocycles on Γ.

This page states functoriality. A K-morphism f: X → Y induces two maps: f_* = Π_1(f): Π_1(X) → Π_1(Y) (37), and f̂ = Π̂_1(f): Π̂_1(X) → Π̂_1(Y) (38). The second map can be obtained from the first by profinite completion. It can also be described purely scheme-theoretically, in terms of finite étale covers / fibre functors of X and Y over the algebraically closed field C. Because of this algebraic description, f̂ is Γ-equivariant: f̂(^uℓ) = ^u(f̂(ℓ)) (39), on the subgroupoids induced on X(K̄) and Y(K̄).

Restricting to the subgroupoids on K-rational points gives immediately (40): f̂(f_ℓ(u)) = f_{f̂(ℓ)}(u) and f̂(g_ℓ(u)) = g_{f̂(ℓ)}(u). That is, the path-cocycles are natural with respect to morphisms of varieties.

The left margin begins an 'autre formulation' involving some T → V, which is illegible. It also gives a variant (40 bis) of the same compatibility, partly illegible.

Purpose: in the Teichmüller/anabelian programme, the action of Galois is 'located' via its action on fundamental groupoids of many test varieties (U_{0,3}, moduli spaces). The coherence of the cocycles under morphisms is what makes the Galois action define an automorphism of a whole 'tower' or diagram of groupoids. This anticipates the Grothendieck–Teichmüller formalism, where compatibility with the morphisms between the M_{g,n} is imposed.
errors: No mathematical error. The Γ-equivariance (39) only makes sense for paths whose endpoints are K̄-points (or tangential base points defined over K̄); the page states this restriction correctly.
Notational clash: f denotes both the morphism X → Y and the cocycle f_ℓ(u). This is harmless but confusing.
The margin formula (40 bis) is only partly legible, so its exact content (which endpoint group, and whether a correction term Π̂_1^Y(u) appears) cannot be checked.

deep.surprise_reason: The page records the routine functoriality and Galois-equivariance of the profinite fundamental groupoid and of the associated path cocycles. It is a natural bookkeeping step in his programme, well known from SGA1 and later Deligne/Ihara work. The illegible margin variant does not appear to contain anything new.
transcription_corrections: 'se borne [-aux-] sous-groupoïdes induits' should read 'se borne aux sous-groupoïdes induits' (the struck word appears to be 'bornes'/'aux' rewritten). Later, 'Si on se [borne] aux sous-groupoïdes induits sur X_K'.

'en termes {+des morphismes+} [-de-] schémas[?] sur X et Y' is more plausibly 'en termes des revêtements / [objets] schématiques sur X et Y', i.e. the étale-cover description over C. The exact words are uncertain.
'et ces derniers commutent : l'action de Γ' — 'ces derniers' refers to the induced maps f̂ restricted to the subgroupoids, which commute with the Γ-action.
Margin: 'Autre formulation, en termes de ... T ... (T → V) ... ' followed by 'Ou (40 bis)'. The formula is roughly 'Π̂^Y(u) g_{f∘ℓ}(u) = f̂(g_ℓ(u))' but is only partly legible.
